verdicts.reason: A scatters the pills across the right side (Tastings top, All Ages middle, a tiny Free Entry jammed against the RSVP button), blows the missing-asset placeholder up into a big focal box, and drops 'Solstice Presents' to the bottom, under its own headline. B at least groups the RSVP and pills in one row, but its text stack is ragged (date and venue offset left, URL centred), the RSVP button carries no more weight than the badges, and the product is a small fragment cut off at the right edge.

A puts the RSVP and badges together in a tidy 2x2 cluster and gives the product real presence on the left, but the cropped missing-asset box sits next to the logo, the RSVP is just one pill among the badges, and 'Solstice Presents' sits below the copy. B has the same ragged left/centre mixed text stack as before, with a weak RSVP lost in the pill row, a tiny product at the edge and the legal text stuck in the top-left corner.

A breaks up every group: Tastings floats above the headline, All Ages hangs at the bottom, Free Entry and RSVP drift on the right, and the logo, product and placeholder shrink to specks in the bottom-right corner, so the brand is effectively lost. B keeps the logo at the top and the CTA and badges together in one row, though its text alignment is ragged and the RSVP has no emphasis.
